outputs.L1: The present disclosure relates to a wearable haptic-pattern display device for a blind person. More particularly, the device has a compact design that facilitates portability and includes a touchscreen disposed on the front surface of a main body. The touchscreen incorporates a touch panel and an electro-sensitive panel integrated and coupled with each other to provide a text screen composed of various combinations of haptic textures. A ring-shaped wearing member is disposed on the rear surface of the main body, allowing a user to wear the member around an index finger and conveniently read, with the thumb, the text screen displayed on the touchscreen. Accordingly, the user can read characters from news, books, or messages regardless of time or location. The device further includes an NFC module disposed within the main body and configured to receive guide information from NFC tags installed at various locations, such as roads, intersections, stores, or existing Braille signs, thereby enabling blind users to make effective use of the guide information.
outputs.L2: This disclosure concerns a compact, portable haptic-pattern display that can be worn by a blind user. A touchscreen on the front of the device’s main body combines an integrated touch panel and electro-sensitive panel to present text through varying arrangements of tactile textures. On the rear of the main body is a ring-shaped attachment designed to fit around the user’s index finger, allowing the user to conveniently feel and interpret the textured text on the touchscreen with the thumb. The device therefore enables characters from news, books, or messages to be read at any time and in any place. The main body also contains an NFC module that receives guidance information from NFC tags positioned at locations such as roads, intersections, shops, and existing braille signs, thereby helping blind users access and make effective use of that information.
outputs.L3:
The disclosure describes a compact, wearable haptic pattern display device intended to improve access to textual and navigational information for blind users. The front of the device includes a touch screen that combines a touch panel with an electro-sensitive panel. By generating different combinations of haptic textures, the screen enables text and other character-based information to be perceived through touch.

A ring-shaped member on the rear of the device allows it to be worn around the index finger. In this position, users can conveniently read the displayed haptic patterns with their thumb, supporting comfortable, one-handed operation. The portable design enables users to access content such as news, books, and messages at any time and in virtually any location.

The device also incorporates an NFC module for receiving location-specific guidance. NFC tags may be installed along roads, at intersections, inside stores, or near existing braille signs. When the device is brought close to one of these tags, it can retrieve the associated guide information and present it through the haptic display, helping users obtain relevant directions and environmental information independently.
outputs.L4:
The compact wearable haptic display is designed to improve access to written information and environmental guidance for blind and visually impaired users. The device combines a touch-sensitive panel with an electro-sensitive haptic panel capable of converting digital text into tactile patterns. These patterns can represent letters, symbols, words, or other meaningful cues, allowing users to perceive information through touch rather than sight.

A finger ring is provided on the rear of the device to support secure, comfortable one-handed use. By placing a finger through the ring, the user can hold the display in the palm and move the thumb across its front surface to read the generated tactile patterns. This arrangement reduces the risk of dropping the device and makes it suitable for use while standing, walking, or traveling. The touch panel may also allow the user to select content, advance through text, return to previous information, or activate device functions through simple thumb gestures.

The display can receive text from connected digital services or compatible electronic devices, enabling users to read news articles, books, personal messages, notices, and other documents whenever needed. Presenting information in a compact tactile format reduces dependence on large embossed materials and allows content to be updated dynamically.

An integrated near-field communication module further supports location-specific services. When the device is brought near a compatible NFC tag installed in a station, public building, bus stop, museum, or other facility, it can receive relevant guidance information. The received data may include place names, directions, route information, platform or room numbers, warnings, and descriptions of nearby facilities. This information is then translated into tactile patterns for private, immediate reading.

By integrating tactile text presentation, touch-based control, a secure wearable structure, and NFC communication in a single portable device, the system gives blind users convenient access to both personal content and public navigation information. It can therefore promote greater independence, mobility, privacy, and participation in everyday activities by making text and environmental guidance available at virtually any time and place.
outputs.L5:
## The Future of NFC

The NFC (Near Field Communication) technology enables devices to exchange information over very short distances. It is commonly used for contactless payments, digital tickets, access cards, and quick device pairing. By holding a smartphone or smartwatch near an NFC reader, users can complete secure transactions within seconds.

NFC is valued for its convenience, speed, and ease of use. Unlike Bluetooth, it does not usually require manual pairing, and its limited range can help reduce unauthorized connections. As smart devices become more widespread, NFC may play an even greater role in transportation, retail, identification, and home automation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a compact wearable haptic text display device for blind users, featuring an integrated touch/electro-sensitive screen, a rear finger ring for thumb reading, and an NFC module that receives guidance from tags in public places.
counterfactuals.output: A compact wearable haptic text display device for blind and visually impaired users includes a housing supporting an integrated touch-sensitive and electro-sensitive screen configured to generate selectively perceptible tactile characters or patterns. A finger ring disposed on a rear surface of the housing secures the device to a user’s finger and positions the screen for reading by the thumb of the same hand. A controller converts text, navigation instructions, alerts, or other information into haptic output presented on the screen and may receive user input through touch gestures. An integrated near-field communication (NFC) module receives location-specific guidance data from NFC tags positioned in public places, including transit facilities, buildings, crossings, and service areas. Upon detection of a tag, the controller causes corresponding directions, identifiers, or safety information to be rendered as thumb-readable tactile output, thereby providing portable, discreet, and accessible wayfinding and text communication.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the present disclosure of a portable assistive device that lets visually impaired people read news, books, messages, and location guidance through tactile patterns.
counterfactuals.output:
The present disclosure relates to a portable assistive device that converts visual and digital information into tactile patterns readable by a visually impaired user. The device may include a camera or scanner for capturing printed text, a processor using optical character recognition to identify the text, and communication interfaces for receiving electronic news, books, messages, and other content.

A tactile output surface—such as a refreshable Braille or configurable raised-pin array—presents the converted information through dynamically generated patterns. The device may also include a positioning module, digital compass, and mapping software to translate location, route, distance, and directional guidance into distinct tactile cues. User controls, voice input, and optional audio feedback can support content selection, navigation, playback speed, and tactile-display settings.

The components may be integrated into a lightweight handheld or wearable housing and operate wirelessly with a mobile phone, remote server, or online content service. In this manner, the device provides private, portable access to printed materials, electronic communications, news, books, and real-time navigation information without requiring reliance on a conventional visual display.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a single-paragraph invention summary for a wearable haptic pattern display with a touchscreen on the front, a ring-shaped wearing member on the back, and NFC support for reading information from roadside, store, intersection, and braille-sign tags.
counterfactuals.output: A wearable haptic pattern display includes a housing having a front-facing touchscreen and a rear-facing, ring-shaped wearing member configured to receive a user’s finger, and an array of tactile actuators arranged to present dynamically generated haptic patterns to the wearer. The device further includes a near-field communication (NFC) module configured to read information from NFC-enabled tags associated with roadside locations, stores, intersections, braille signs, or other objects and environments. A controller processes the received information and causes the tactile actuators to output corresponding braille characters, symbols, directional cues, alerts, or other discernible patterns, while the touchscreen provides visual information and user input controls. The invention thereby enables portable, discreet, and accessible delivery of location-based, navigational, commercial, and textual information through touch.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Korean-patent-style English abstract for an assistive wearable device that enables a blind person to access tactile text anywhere and obtain navigation or facility information through NFC tags.
counterfactuals.output: The present invention relates to an assistive wearable device for enabling a visually impaired person to access tactile text and obtain navigation or facility information. The device comprises a wearable body, a tactile display unit configured to selectively form raised characters, an NFC communication unit configured to read information from an NFC tag installed at a location or facility, and a controller configured to convert text received from a user terminal or the NFC tag into tactile output. When the device approaches the NFC tag, the controller identifies location, route, facility, or guidance information stored in or linked to the NFC tag and provides the information through the tactile display unit and, optionally, a voice or vibration output unit. Accordingly, a visually impaired user may read electronic text in various environments and independently obtain context-specific navigation and facility information without requiring visual interaction.
